_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: "The input" is the message input [data-testid="message-input"]; "the send button" is [data-testid="send-button"]; "the chevron" is the send options button [data-testid="send-options-button"]; "the thinking indicator" is [data-testid="agent-thinking"]; "the Stop button" is button[aria-label="Stop"]; "queued badges" are [data-testid="queued-badge"]. "Tap X" means a touch step "start" on X immediately followed by a touch step "end" (a tap, not a click). "Send X and wait for work" means: fill the input with X; the send button should become enabled (up to 5s); tap it; the thinking indicator should become visible (up to 30s). "Queue X" means: fill the input with X; the chevron should be enabled and visible (up to 5s each); tap it; the queue option [data-testid="queue-option"] should become visible (up to 5s); tap it. Every test starts: navigate to /c/queue and wait (up to 30s) for the input to be visible. Stopping the agent restores a queued message whose request the server has not accepted yet. Queueing requests (/chat requests whose JSON body has queue true) are held back until call "release queue"; call "queue started" reports "true" once one has reached the server. 1. Navigate to /c/queue and wait for the input. 2. Send "delay: 60" and wait for work. 3. Queue "echo: pending steering". 4. Call "queue started"; it should become "true". 5. Tap the Stop button. 6. The input's value should be exactly "echo: pending steering". 7. Call "release queue".
